supp-a-ratios-and-hat-matrix: Appendix A 1, p.22: the paper defines hat P_N = P + N^(-1/2) hat Xi (N training shots, M test shots) and the ratios gamma_out = d^2/n_out, gamma_tr = d^2/n_tr, gamma_Q = n_out/n_tr as notation.
supp-lemma-a1-haar-squared-expectation: Lemma A1, Appendix A 2, p.23: the proof is in the paper. It writes Tr(D sigma) = v_D^T v_sigma and applies the Haar second moment (A3) to get (Tr(D^2) + (Tr D)^2)/(d(d+1)), then splits D into its traceless part. The Haar integration formula is a textbook tool used as a step. No cited paper result is used.
supp-definition-1-target-ensembles: Definition 1, Appendix A 2, p.23: the paper defines the admissible targets O = c_O I + O_0 with Tr(O_0^2) = d Delta^2 > 0 and |c_O|/sqrt(d Delta^2) <= C, drawn independently of apparatus, states and counts, with the three direction laws. The shared isotropic moments (A8) follow from eq. (A2) for law (iii) and by direct computation for (i) and (ii); the computation is elementary and not shown.
supp-lemma-b1-gaussian-lift: Lemma B1, Appendix B 1, p.24: stated with its conditions (n_out >= d) and proved there. The proof uses the Wishart estimate (Lemma G3, Gaussian singular-value concentration, textbook, Vershynin [24]), Wick's identity, and a nonzero-polynomial-minor argument for the almost-sure rank. No specific other paper's theorem is a step.
supp-lemma-b2-effect-traces: Lemma B2, Appendix B 1, p.25: proved in the paper. omega_a = X/(X+Y) with X ~ Gamma(d), Y ~ Gamma(n_out - d) gives the Beta law. The Chernoff bound for Gamma variables (eq. B6) and a union bound give (B4). Taking epsilon proportional to sqrt(log n_out / d) gives (B5). I checked the constants (4 epsilon, 4 n_out exp(-epsilon^2 d/3)). Only textbook tools are used.
supp-mp-law-definition: Appendix B 2, p.25, eq. (B7): the paper defines mu_MP,gamma with the (1 - 1/gamma)_+ atom at zero and the bulk density on [lambda_-, lambda_+], lambda_pm = (1 pm sqrt(gamma))^2. It states that the atom counts inaccessible directions and the lower edge reaches zero at gamma = 1 (lambda_- = 0 there).
supp-theorem-b1-rank-and-zero-modes: Theorem B1, Appendix B 2, p.24 (printed p.26): the rank assertion 'follows from Lemma B1' (almost-sure rank X = min(d^2, n_out), T invertible). The zero-eigenvalue counts (d^2 - n_out)_+ and (n_out - d^2)_+ follow directly. This part of the theorem does not use the Marchenko-Pastur step.
supp-outlier-gram-row-sums: Proof of Theorem B1, Appendix B 2, p.26, eqs. (B11), (B12): G_mu has nonnegative entries and row sums omega_a (since sum_b Tr(mu_a mu_b) = Tr(mu_a)). The Rayleigh quotient on the uniform vector is (1/n_out) sum omega_a = d/n_out, and the norm is at most the largest row sum, which gives (B11). M_mu 1 = v_Id and M_mu^T v_Id = omega give (B12). The event of Lemma B2 bounds both. I checked each step; only Lemma B2 (textbook tools) is used.
supp-lemma-b3-no-extremal-edge-claim: Appendix B 4, p.29: the paper states that the upper-frame bounds used in the fixed-rank peak examples do not rely on weak spectral convergence and do not assert an extremal-edge limit. This is a statement of what the paper claims and does not claim. (The bounds themselves rest on Lemmas G7 and G8, which cite Tikhomirov [47]; this item does not grade those bounds.)
supp-theorem-c1-proof-reduction: Proof of Theorem C1, Appendix C 2, p.31, eqs. (C9) to (C12): the exact average (C9), the bounds (C10), (C11) and the identity-target estimate are shown line by line. They use Haar moments (A2), (A3), the trace concentration of Lemma B2, and projector contractions. I checked that the removed identity contribution is at most 1/[d(d^2 - 1)]. This reduction step uses no cited paper result.
supp-lemma-c2-shot-averaged-ls: Lemma C2, Appendix C 4, p.33: proved by direct expectation of the multinomial counts (E n = N p, Cov = N Sigma). I checked item 4 line by line: n Sigma(p-bar) - Pi = diag delta - (1 delta^T + delta 1^T + delta delta^T)/n has norm at most epsilon + 2 epsilon + epsilon^2, and the between-state term is at most K^2/[d(d+1)]. No cited result is used.
supp-lemma-c2-scope-not-concentration: Appendix C 4, p.33: the paper states that Lemma C2 concerns averages at fixed training states, and that identifying eta = 1 with a single record needs the realized matrices of eq. (C22) to concentrate, 'which we do not prove; near n_out = n_tr they do not (section E 3 b)'. This is a limit the paper states on its own result.
supp-d-physical-ridge-readout: Appendix D 1 a, p.34, eq. (D1): the paper defines the physical ridge readout, eta = n_out N tau, and states that at tau = 0 it is the minimum-Euclidean-norm least-squares solution (hat w_N,0 = (hat P_N^T)^+ y).
supp-d-signal-in-shot-noise-units: Appendix D 1 b, p.35, eq. (D5): the paper defines the rescaled traceless measurement matrix and states that a direction with rescaled frame eigenvalue x has squared singular value alpha_d x, alpha_d = N/[d(d+1)]. The Lemma D1 interpretation is the paper's own reading of that definition; the scaling itself is exact (checked against (D5)).
supp-d-proportional-limit-ratios: Appendix D 1 c, p.36, eq. (D10) and the text after it: the paper sets the proportional-limit ratios kappa_d, gamma_d, alpha_d, and states that kappa < 1 or > 1 places n_out above or below informational completeness, that outcome count alone does not assert full rank, that the peak asymptotics take kappa != 1 while the fixed-ridge comparison holds for every kappa > 0, and that the centered matrix is square at n_out = n_tr.
supp-d-empirical-bounds-assumptions: Appendix D 1 c, p.36, eqs. (D11) to (D13): the paper states these as its assumptions (frame bounds by K, covariance bounds between c and K, liminf of the normalized trace positive for a nonzero variance amplitude), with the sentence that for random states or apparatuses they are imposed on events of probability tending to one.
supp-d-uniform-weight-elimination: Appendix D 2 a, p.37, eqs. (D14), (D15): exact algebra in the paper. P-hat^T 1 = 1 splits the loss into a centered part plus (w0 + p-hat^T w_perp - y-bar)^2 + n_out tau w0^2, and minimizing over w0 gives the penalty n_out tau/(1 + n_out tau) times the squared mean residual. That the correction vanishes from normalized traces at fixed ridge is shown later: Z_eta - K-hat has rank one and bounded norm (Lemma D6), giving the O((d^2-1)^(-1)) difference (D63). I checked the algebra.
supp-d-centered-costs-definition: Appendix D 2 b, p.38, eqs. (D22), (D23): the paper defines F_eta,d (normalized centered test variance) and G_eta,d (normalized traceless reconstruction cost), and states that at strong ridge the centered prediction vanishes, so F tends to 0 and G tends to 1 (the weights go to zero, which gives that directly).
supp-lemma-d2-balanced-probabilities: Lemma D2, Appendix D 2 b, p.39: proved from the covariance bounds. The diagonal bounds give c/2 <= n_out p_a(1 - p_a) <= K, so p_a >= c/(2 n_out); summing the other entries bounds 1 - p_a below; rho_i <= I gives p_ai <= Tr(mu_a) = d p_I/d,a <= K d/n_out. I checked each step.
supp-lemma-d3-multinomial-gaussian: Lemma D3, Appendix D 2 b, pp.38 to 40: proved in the paper by shot-wise Lindeberg replacement with a block-inverse bound, the Efron-Stein variance inequality, Gaussian integration by parts, a rank-one bridge to a common covariance, and concavity for the derivatives. All are textbook tools; no specific other paper's theorem is a step. The proof is condensed (several o(1) bounds are stated, not expanded). The limit that the replacement does not control the smallest singular values is stated in the lemma's text.
supp-lemma-d5-exact-restoration: Lemma D5, Appendix D 3, pp.42, 43: proved in the paper. Eliminating w0 in (D14) adds beta_eta b_N b_N^T to the centered normal matrix, and Sherman-Morrison gives (D45) to (D47); substitution gives (D48) to (D50). At zero ridge the minimum-norm criterion fixes the nullspace correction by minimizing (D53), giving (D51), (D52). Only algebra is used; no cited paper result.
supp-lemma-d6-mean-correction-size: Lemma D6, Appendix D 3, p.43: proved from the empirical bounds, the ridge-filter bounds ||Q-hat P-hat^c|| <= 1/(2 sqrt(eta)), ||Q-hat|| <= 1/eta, J_eta >= 1, and the mean-size estimates (D55), (D56). No cited paper result is used. The proof is short but each bound is derived.
supp-lemma-d7-diffuse-mean: Lemma D7, Appendix D 3, p.43: proved by purity. For an eigenvector of rho-bar with eigenvalue lambda, the mean squared length of (rho_i - rho-bar) applied to it is lambda - lambda^2. Summing d matrix-entry variances against the upper frame bound gives lambda(1 - lambda) <= K d/[d(d+1)]. The positive average-trace condition (D13) keeps Tr(rho-bar^2), hence lambda_max, away from one, so every eigenvalue is O(1/d). I checked the steps.
supp-lemma-d8-identity-label-readout: Lemma D8, Appendix D 3, p.44: proved in the paper. The coefficient bounds follow from Lemma D5 (the readout is the orthogonal-complement part beta_eta Q-hat b_N / J_eta with J_eta >= 1 and ||Q-hat|| <= 1/eta); the zero-ridge case uses the same bound with the nullspace projector; the variance and ideal-test bounds use (D55), the covariance upper bound and the Haar split (D2). No cited paper result is used.
supp-proposition-e1-block-form: Proposition E1, Appendix E 1, p.46: proved by block elimination. The interpolation conditions are multiplied by [V1 V2]^T, V2^T y = (M_rho V2)^T v_O = 0 since M_mu^T is injective for an informationally complete POVM, which gives eq. (16) and then eq. (E1). U2 spans ker P^T and M_rho is injective, so M_mu U2 = 0 and the observable depends only on w1. Conditions (IC POVM, spanning states, n_out = n_tr, invertible blocks) are carried in the quotes. No cited paper result is used.
supp-e1-critical-equation-existence: Appendix E 1 a, p.47, eqs. (E2) to (E7): the proof is in the paper and uses only elementary steps. Each term 1/(zeta + lambda_j) decreases strictly in zeta. At zeta = 1 the average is at most one. S has rank at most d^2 - 1 on the (n_out - 1)-dimensional space, so at least n_out - d^2 eigenvalues vanish, and the average at zeta = 1 - kappa_d is at least (n_out - d^2)/((n_out - 1)(1 - kappa_d)) = 1. No cited result is used. The below-completeness remark is a scope statement.
supp-remark-e1-trace-regularity: Remark E1, Appendix E 1 a, p.47: the paper states the extra assumptions its rounded-profile results need (limits of the fixed-ridge normalized traces and first derivatives, and local convergence at the critical point with limits continuous as gamma tends to 1) and that 'mere existence of fixed-ridge limits does not supply this additional critical regularity'. That is a stated limit on what its results cover.
supp-e2-flat-noise-assumption: Appendix E 2, p.51, eq. (E25): the paper states that all examples assume flat categorical covariances. It states h = zeta_* and C_V = alpha H_*, which agree with the flat-noise note after (E10). It states that the coefficients describe the centered singularity and that the physical error follows (D62).
supp-e3a-limiting-law-no-smallest-eigenv: Appendix E 3 a, p.54: the paper says the hard-edge statements concern the limiting law and 'do not control the smallest empirical eigenvalues'. It says the law alone does not control finite-dimensional pseudoinverses. It says small singular directions give a peak only when their labels carry weight, matching (E40), (E41). All three are caveats on its own results.
supp-e3a-label-strength-and-lower-bound: Appendix E 3 a, p.54: the sentence states what the below-completeness result does not cover, namely that a square matrix alone does not force a peak for every target. The paper states it directly after (E41).
supp-e3c-positive-critical-root-conditio: Appendix E 3 c, p.56, (E50)-(E52): f_d(zeta) = avg 1/(zeta + lambda_j) is strictly decreasing with f_d(1) <= 1. A positive root of f_d = 1 therefore exists iff the limit of f_d at 0 exceeds 1, with equality a boundary case. I checked that d_eff = (n_out-1)(1-zeta) is equivalent for zeta > 0. The proportional theorem's extra requirements are stated separately. No cited result is used.
supp-e3c-geometry-mean-assumptions: Appendix E 3 c, pp.55-56, eq. (E49) and the text after it: the paper states the hypotheses kappa > 1, kappa gamma > 1 (both n_out, n_tr < d^2), the liminf trace condition (positive ideal-test amplitude) and q_d going to 0 (removes the mean contribution). It says random states or apparatuses need these to hold with probability tending to one.
supp-theorem-e3-proof-physical-costs-sco: Proof of Thm E3, p.57: for a traceless isotropic target the constant-prediction term is ||t_eta||^2/(d^2-1) by (D50). Lemma D6 (proved on p.43 from Lemma D5 with no cited theorem) bounds it by O_P(q_d + 1/(d^2-1)), so it goes to zero when q_d goes to 0. The paper then states 'We do not claim this replacement' for a general target with an identity component or an empirical-mean correction.
supp-e3c-order-of-limits-scope: Appendix E 3 c, p.57, 'Order of limits and physical scope': the paper states that dimensions must grow at fixed ridge before (gamma, eta) goes to (1, 0). It states that a full zero-penalty profile at gamma != 1 needs weighted inverse-tail control (E22) and that minimum-norm divergence at interpolation needs none. It states that without q_d going to 0 the centered profiles hold but the physical error keeps its mean term.
supp-e3d-targets-outside-peak-regime: Appendix E 3 d, p.60, 'Targets and geometries outside the peak regime': the paper lists cases its peak result does not cover. These are well-represented labels (no peak despite a hard edge), a zero traceless Born map (C_G = 0, which follows from (E9)), collapsed training fluctuations that violate noncollapse, and the region outside the positive-root regime, which needs separate spectral analysis.
supp-f1-proof-gaussian-pairs-lemma-g10: Proof of Prop F1, p.62: the paper states what the proof does (evaluates the three traces with Gaussian pairs of the same joint covariance via Lemma G10). It states that the original Haar regression residual is not assumed independent. It states that this does not remove the separate inverse-tail requirement at zero penalty. These are statements of method and limit, not a claim to be proved.
supp-f2-exact-haar-absence: Proof of Prop F2, p.63: a row of a normalized Haar isometry has squared norm W ~ Beta(d, n_out-d). A Haar pure state has overlap U ~ Beta(1, d-1) with it, independently of W. So the outcome probability is WU, a record misses the row with probability E_U (1-WU)^N, and the n_tr records are independent given W. Exchangeability of the rows gives (F13).
supp-f2-absence-rate-expansion: Appendix F 2, p.63: (F14) is proved from X = n_out W/d going to Gamma(d, rate d), E U = 1/d and the Gamma Laplace transform. The rate -N^-1 log u = (d/N) log(1 + N/(d gamma)) expands to 1/gamma - N/(2 d gamma^2) + O(N^2/(d^2 gamma^3)), which I checked. The remarks on (F13) and (F14) follow.
supp-lemma-g1-spectral-comparisons: Lemma G1, p.64: stated with conditions and proved by singular-value inequalities, Cauchy interlacing and Courant-Fischer with rank-k intersection. These are textbook tools. The dimension shift gives (G2) and the k/p bound on the distribution functions.
supp-lemma-g2-negative-second-moment: Lemma G2, p.64: the Schur complement of the Gram matrix gives (G^-1)_aa = dist(y_a, H_a)^-2, and summing over a gives the trace. The proof is complete and elementary.
supp-lemma-g4-quadratic-form-gaussian-li: Lemma G4, p.65: Wick's identity gives E F = Tr(H) and the Gaussian Poincare inequality gives Var F <= C E[||g||^2 ||gg^dagger - I||_F^2] = O(d^3). Chebyshev then gives d^-2(m^dagger H m - Tr H) going to 0 in probability. The Gaussian Poincare inequality is a textbook tool.
supp-lemma-g5-lifted-distances: Lemma G5, pp.65-66: the conditional mean comes from the Gamma/uniform decomposition and the Haar moment (A3). The tail combines Levy concentration on the sphere (textbook), a Chernoff bound (B6) and a union bound. The constants are universal as stated.
supp-lemma-g9-population-covariance-inte: Lemma G9, p.67 (rendered): stated with its conditions, including the uniform quadratic-form concentration (G12). It is proved by the leave-one-column and Sherman-Morrison reduction, the traced normal equation on spectral projectors, and existence and uniqueness from the strictly increasing right side of 1 = w + y integral wt/(xi + wt) dH. It cites no external theorem. The proof is compressed but covers every claim, derivatives included.

corollary-2-proof: Section 3.2.1, p.24: for a known accept instance xA, an unbounded algorithm can simulate OP(xA), so Theorem 1 applies, and constrained verifiers cannot do better. The argument is complete; the cited lower bounds enter only in the corollary's examples.
corollary-5-proof-reduction: Section 3.2.2, pp.24-25: the reduction is in full. If D is a parity distribution the learner's s equals s' (loss at most 1/4 forces s = s'), so the estimate is at most 1/8; if D is uniform every s has loss 1/2, so the estimate lies in [3/8, 5/8]. nisq-observation-noisy-oracle: Section 3.3, p.27: follows from the definition of the NISQ-lambda model as an algorithm with a noisy copy oracle, as the proof of Corollary 6 shows.
theorem-6-protocol-rounds: Section 4.2, pp.30-31 defines the protocol's compute, pure test and mixed test rounds.
theorem-6-algorithm-1-parameters: Algorithm 1, p.32 gives N, delta-tilde and m and the verifier's decision rule.
theorem-6-completeness: Section 4.2, p.31: per-round success at least 1 - delta-tilde, union bound N*delta-tilde = delta/2. The SWAP-test copy count is textbook ([Buh+01]).
theorem-6-soundness-concentration: Section 4.2, p.31, Eq. 6: union bound plus Hoeffding, 3exp(-N/72) <= delta/2 by the choice of N (checked). The text writes the event as 's_i not equal s', which is a typo for 's_i = s'; the computation is for the count of rounds of type s.
theorem-6-soundness-indistinguishability: Section 4.2, pp.32-33: indistinguishability of computation and test rounds (a maximally mixed state, or a state randomised by an m-design), then a guessing bound 2^(-N/4) <= delta/2, using C(N/2, N/4) >= 2^(N/4). It is in the paper.
